narrative:
The model predicts you have a 42% chance of failing your final year, which is high enough that the school requires you to take remedial courses to help you graduate.

The prediction is driven mainly by three key aspects of your situation. By far the strongest factor is that you have already failed two classes in the past. Among students who passed, the average number of previous failures is zero, so this history strongly pushes the model toward expecting you to fail again. The second most important factor is that your guardian is someone other than a parent. This actually works slightly in your favor compared with most students who pass, whose guardian is almost always a parent. The third factor is your very low weekend alcohol consumption. This also mildly helps your prediction, since students who pass tend to report higher weekend drinking on average.

Even though having a non-parent guardian and drinking very little on weekends are positive signals, they are not strong enough to overcome the heavy negative influence of your two past failures. 

To improve, focus first on breaking the pattern of failing classes. Speak with your teachers about targeted support in the subjects that have been hardest for you, create a realistic study schedule, and use the remedial courses to close any remaining gaps before the final exams. Small, consistent changes now can still change the outcome.
